verses.english: Linked Discourses 55.42
5. Overflowing Merit, With Verses
Overflowing Merit (2nd)
“Mendicants, there are these four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.
What four?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
verses.english: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

verses.pali: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.

verses.english: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati muttacāgo payatapāṇi vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṁvibhāgarato.
verses.english: Furthermore, a noble disciple lives at home rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.
This is the fourth kind of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

verses.pali: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puññābhisandā, kusalābhisandā, sukhassāhārā.
verses.english: These are the four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.

verses.pali: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi puññābhisandehi kusalābhisandehi samannāgatassa ariyasāvakassa na sukaraṁ puññassa pamāṇaṁ gaṇetuṁ:
verses.english: When a noble disciple has these four kinds of overflowing merit and goodness, it’s not easy to count how much merit they have by saying that
this is the extent of their overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

verses.pali: Atha kho asaṅkhyeyyo appameyyo mahāpuññakkhandhotveva saṅkhyaṁ gacchati.
verses.english: It’s simply reckoned as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of merit.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yatthimā mahānadiyo saṁsandanti samenti, seyyathidaṁ—
verses.english: There are places where the great rivers—the Ganges, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī—join together and converge.

verses.pali: gaṅgā, yamunā, aciravatī, sarabhū, mahī, tattha na sukaraṁ udakassa pamāṇaṁ gaṇetuṁ:
verses.english: It’s not easy to count how much water is in such places by saying

verses.pali: ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakānī’ti vā ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakasatānī’ti vā ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakasahassānī’ti vā ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakasatasahassānī’ti vāti.
verses.english: how many gallons, how many hundreds, thousands, hundreds of thousands of gallons there are.

verses.pali: Atha kho asaṅkhyeyyo appameyyo mahāudakakkhandhotveva saṅkhyaṁ gacchati.
verses.english: It’s simply reckoned as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of water.

verses.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, imehi catūhi puññābhisandehi kusalābhisandehi samannāgatassa ariyasāvakassa na sukaraṁ puññassa pamāṇaṁ gaṇetuṁ:
verses.english: In the same way, when a noble disciple has these four kinds of overflowing merit and goodness, it’s not easy to count how much merit they have by saying that
this is the extent of their overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

verses.pali: Atha kho asaṅkhyeyyo appameyyo mahāpuññakkhandhotveva saṅkhyaṁ gacchatī”ti.
verses.english: It’s simply reckoned as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of merit.”
That is what the Buddha said.
Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“Hosts of people use the rivers,
and though the rivers are many,
all reach the great deep, the boundless ocean,
the cruel sea that’s home to precious gems.
So too, when a person gives food, drink, and clothes;
and they’re a giver of beds, seats, and mats—
the streams of merit reach that astute person,
as the rivers bring their waters to the sea.”
